A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Puffin and Puffin-4M. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison. Retained material can be matched despite relocation and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original camera-understanding and controllable-generation evaluations, ablations, and qualitative downstream results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds FID measurements, baseline retraining, computational-cost and training analyses, and multi-turn examples.

M1.justification: The encoder/LLM/diffusion architecture, camera-map conditioning, thinking procedure, and four-stage training recipe remain unchanged. The expanded tokenization explanation and multi-turn demonstrations do not document a new algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: Figure A3 adds multi-turn evaluation scenarios connecting understanding to generation and generation to understanding through previous conversational outputs. The training domains, named benchmarks, and existing single-view and cross-view tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table A4 adds a separately evaluated GeoCalib* variant retrained on Puffin-4M alongside the original GeoCalib and Puffin. Existing comparison rosters are retained. This adds a trained baseline variant, not a new comparator architecture; Bagel is discussed without a performance evaluation.

E3.justification: v2 adds FID evaluation, computational-cost comparisons, and a control retraining GeoCalib on Puffin-4M using its original recipe. Original benchmark settings remain unchanged. A new Stage-II experiment is described as varying data size, but Figure A2(b) labels its horizontal axes 'Iterations', leaving the precise manipulation unclear.

E4.justification: New Appendix A2.3 substantially expands the analytical questions beyond the retained architecture, thinking, camera-map, and joint-training ablations. It adds a model-versus-data investigation through GeoCalib retraining and a purported data-scaling study, computational-cost and error-distribution comparisons, and multi-turn case studies.

E5.justification: Figure A2(a) newly reports box-and-whisker error distributions for GeoCalib and Puffin on MegaDepth and Puffin-Und. The whisker conventions are unspecified, and no repeated-run counts, seeds, or confidence levels are added. These plots therefore do not establish uncertainty across training runs.

E6.justification: Original camera-error scores remain unchanged, but substantial new results cover visual quality, cost, retraining, training curves, and multi-turn behavior. Table 4 newly reports FID of 69.46 for Puffin versus 90.91 for PreciseCam. Table A4 adds retrained GeoCalib median roll/pitch/FoV errors of 1.12/2.54/5.47 degrees under the new training condition; these are not changes to the original baseline scores.

T1.justification: The task definitions, Perspective Field equation, and parameter-to-photographic-term mapping in Table A1 are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions: unified camera understanding and generation, thinking with camera, and Puffin-4M. Additional evaluations support these claims without redefining their scope. The release-status update concerns reproducibility information.

C2.justification: New discussion attributes retrained GeoCalib's weaker results to limited capacity, argues that Puffin needs large-scale data, and interprets differing roll/pitch/FoV trends. It also discusses deployment versus computational cost and interleaved interaction. Existing fixed-resolution, cropping, and evaluator limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 clarifies numerical-parameter tokenization, and Table A3 adds parameter counts and GFLOPs. The abstract changes a promised code/model/pipeline/benchmark release to a reported release, although Section 5.3 retains future-tense benchmark wording. Actual availability cannot be verified from the PDFs; core implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Deng et al. (2025), associated with Bagel, and discusses Puffin's size and cost relative to general-purpose and specialized models. The main related-work survey and novelty positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: v2 adds Appendix A2.3, renumbers downstream applications to A2.4, expands tokenization and joint-training explanations, and makes small abstract, author-note, and acknowledgment edits. The overall narrative structure and most existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables A3–A4 and Figures A2–A3, extends Table 4 with a FID column, and relocates some existing displays. Earlier appendix Figures A2–A9 become A4–A11 with their illustrations retained. These are localized additions and layout adjustments rather than a visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the added visual-quality measurements, computational-cost disclosure, and same-data baseline retraining make the empirical assessment more informative. The gain is limited by reporting weaknesses: Figure A2(b) describes data scaling while plotting iterations, and the error-distribution whiskers are undefined. The revision adds useful evidence without fully resolving the model-versus-data explanation or statistical reliability.
